summary: Venusaur is a 2 m, 100 kg grassland quadruped carrying a large flower on its back, and it runs partly on sunlight: the spread petals catch the sun's rays and fill its body with power, so it is strongest in summer and keeps moving to find sun. Its flower gives off a fragrance that soothes people and calms animals in the middle of a fight, strongest after rain, and the scent draws other Pokémon to it. The line begins as Bulbasaur, which hatches with a seed on its back and lives off the seed's stored nutrients while it is young. No Gen I–IV game has the line in the wild; every Venusaur is raised from a starter Bulbasaur.

anatomy.text: A heavy quadruped of 2.0 m and 100 kg, Grass and Poison type.
A large flower grows on its back; its broad petals spread to catch the sun's rays.
In Ivysaur, the legs and trunk grow thick and strong to bear the weight of the bulb; once the bulb is large it seems unable to stand on its hind legs.
Bulbasaur's seed is filled with nutrients, and its bulb stores energy.

diet.text: It converts sunlight into energy through the flower on its back.
It also eats: Bulbasaur 'can go for days without eating a single morsel', which only makes sense for an animal that normally eats. What it eats is never said.
So the line is a mixotroph, combining sunlight with food. How much of its energy comes from each is unknown.
diet.analogy: The sea slug Elysia chlorotica keeps chloroplasts from the algae it eats and can live partly on the sugars they make in sunlight.

diet.text: The young live first on the seed: while it is young, Bulbasaur grows on the nutrients stored in the seed on its back.
diet.analogy: As a germinating seed's stored reserves feed the seedling until it can photosynthesise, except that here the seed feeds the animal.

diet.text: Ivysaur's bulb grows as it absorbs nutrients and draws energy, so the plant on its back is fed by the animal as well as by the sun.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: grassland.
It needs sun: it stays on the move to seek sunlight, so open, unshaded country suits it best.
Not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Bulbasaur is a starter gift in Pallet Town (Red, Blue, FireRed, LeafGreen, and HeartGold and SoulSilver after beating Red) and in Cerulean City in Yellow.

behavior.text: Diurnal and sun-following: it moves about to stay in sunlight and is more powerful in summer.
Its petals release a pleasant fragrance as it warms itself in the sun.
The juveniles bask: Bulbasaur naps in bright sunlight, and Ivysaur spends more and more time lying in the sun as its bud nears blooming.

social.text: No entry describes groups or pairs.
Its scent, stronger after rain, attracts other Pokémon; which ones, and why, is not said.

reproduction.text: Monster and Grass egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male; the sex ratio is shared with the other starter lines and is probably a game convention.
Every Bulbasaur has a seed on its back from the day it is born.
Whether Venusaur's flower sets seed, and whether that seed is the one each Bulbasaur carries, is the obvious question and nowhere answered.

defense.text: Its fragrance calms those engaged in battle.
Poison Powder and Sleep Powder (both Lv 13 by level-up) are powders, presumably from the plant, that poison or put attackers to sleep; it is Grass and Poison typed.
Its size and weight alone discourage most attackers; no predator is named.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.
Following the sun implies it can sense light and warmth on its body or flower.

life_cycle.text: Bulbasaur (0.7 m, 6.9 kg) becomes Ivysaur at level 16 (1.0 m, 13 kg) and Venusaur at level 32 (2.0 m, 100 kg), a near eightfold jump in mass at the last step.
The plant grows with the animal: the seed grows steadily larger as the body grows, sprouting into a bulb.
Sunlight adds to Ivysaur's strength and makes its bud grow; when the bud swells and smells sweet, the large flower is about to bloom.
The bud gives off an aroma when it is ready to bloom and a pleasant one once it has bloomed.

Read as development: seed (stored food) in Bulbasaur, bud in Ivysaur, flower in Venusaur, with the animal moving from living on its seed to living partly on sunlight; the bloom and the evolution to Venusaur seem to be the same event.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Sunlight: Growth (Lv 28), Synthesis (Lv 45) and Solar Beam (Lv 53) all draw on light, matching the solar-energy entries.
Scent: Sweet Scent (Lv 23) is the attracting aroma of 3.10 in move form, and in the field it draws wild Pokémon out.
Petal Dance is learned at Lv 32, the level at which it evolves and the flower blooms.

Plant weapons: Leech Seed (Lv 7), Vine Whip (Lv 9), Razor Leaf (Lv 20) and Worry Seed (Lv 39). Leech Seed, which plants a seed that drains the target, hints that the line can sow seeds on other animals.

ecology.text: Partly a primary producer: it makes energy from sunlight, so it sits low in the food web (trophic level about 1.5) even though it also eats.
Its scent draws other Pokémon. If those include pollinators, the flower could be pollinated by them; if they include grazers or predators, it would be a hazard. Neither is described.
ecology.note: 3.10 says only that the scent attracts other Pokémon.

humans.text: The flower's aroma soothes people's emotions.
In the games the line reaches people only as a starter.

homestead.text: A calming presence: its aroma soothes people and calms animals that are fighting, which makes it a candidate for the Hearth hall or a busy yard.
A lure: Sweet Scent, its own level-up move, draws wild Pokémon out, useful for census work or catching.
Its weakest season is winter: it is strongest in summer sun, so on Blackthorn's short, cold days it would need the Glasshouse.
Heavy work: at 2 m and 100 kg, with Strength from a machine, it can pull or push loads.
Keep its poison and sleep powders in mind around grazing animals and their fodder.
Bulbasaur raised here would need sunny ground to bask on; a young one that rarely sees sun may grow slowly.

niche.foraging: basks and moves to follow the sun; juveniles draw on stored seed nutrients; some ordinary eating is implied but not described

relationships.note: After rain its scent is stronger; whether rain matters to it otherwise is not said.
Only the attraction is canon. If the visitors pollinate the flower, this is a mutualism; if not, it may be nothing of the kind.

ecotypes.name: Rooted meadow-sitter
ecotypes.reading: Ingrain puts down roots that feed the user but stop it fleeing, Curse trades speed for toughness, and Amnesia steadies its resistance. Together they describe a lineage that stops following the sun and roots instead, the reverse of 3.1's 'stays on the move'. Fits rich, reliably sunny meadows where staying put pays.
ecotypes.behavior: Settles into one sunny patch for weeks and won't be moved.

ecotypes.name: Lullaby bloom
ecotypes.reading: Grass Whistle is a soothing melody that puts the listener to sleep, Charm softens an attacker, and Safeguard protects against status harm. A lineage that pacifies rather than fights, extending the calming aroma of 3.8 to sound. Fits meadows shared with many large grazers, or a homestead.
ecotypes.behavior: Hums and wafts scent until the quarrel around it stops.

ecotypes.name: Shade bramble
ecotypes.reading: Sludge is a poisonous splash and Power Whip a heavy lash of vines. A lineage that spends less on basking and more on defence, poisoning and whipping what comes close. Fits damp, part-shaded woodland edges where sunlight is short and the plant on its back can't carry it alone.
ecotypes.behavior: Sits low in the undergrowth and lashes out with vines.

open_questions: What does the line eat, and how much of its energy comes from sunlight?
Does Venusaur's flower set seed, and is that where Bulbasaur's seed comes from?
Is the seed 'planted' at birth (1.1) or simply present from birth (1.4, 1.7)?
Which Pokémon does its scent attract, and do they pollinate it?
How does it cope with highland winters, short days and snow cover?
Are the animal and the plant one organism, or two in partnership?

contradictions.note: Red, Blue and LeafGreen (1.1) say a strange seed was planted on its back at birth, implying something does the planting; Silver, SoulSilver and FireRed (1.4, 1.7) say it carries the seed from the day it is born, implying it is born with it.

folklore.text: Venusaur's flower is said to take on vivid colours if it gets plenty of nutrition and sunlight.
folklore.note: Reported belief; plausible for a plant, but not stated as fact.

folklore.text: Ivysaur's bulb is said to blossom into a large flower when it absorbs nutrients.
folklore.note: Line folklore. Other entries state the blooming as fact (2.6, 2.9).
